title: citesNameAsHandover treats a handover phrase inside reported speech as a real handover: "He said over to you, Nikhil, and left." returns true
evidence: found while writing speaker-relation-rules.test.ts for u2-4-phase3-resume-c2; the reported() guard only checks said/says/asks-me immediately before the NAME, not a handover phrase that follows a reporting verb earlier in the clause. Not one of the recorded ISS-104/282/289 reproductions; the c1 replay corpus and the 8 recorded wrong links are unaffected.
fix_direction: extend reported() to look back one clause for a reporting verb (said/says/told/asked) before the handover cue, with a recorded-reproduction test. File-don't-fix per the low-severity rule.
checker_note: checker u2-4-phase3-resume-c2 cycle 2: severity raised low -> critical. Reproduced END TO END through extractSpeakers, not only at the predicate: turns [spk:1 "He said over to you, Nikhil, and left.", spk:0 "I think so, yes.", spk:1 "ok"] with injected complete [{speakerRef:'spk:0',displayName:'Nikhil',turnIds:['t1']}] SHIPS spk:0 -> Nikhil. Also ships for "Someone said: over to you, Nikhil." and "The chair told me earlier that it was over to you, Nikhil." Reported speech naming a person publishes that name under the next speaker: the same class as critical ISS-282/ISS-104. The maker's note that it is not in a recorded reproduction does not lower the class.

title: citesNameAsHandover and citesNameAsThanks never call hasNamingCueAt, so the place-versus-person signal and the ISS-255 handover refusal are bypassed on the new relation route: the recorded ISS-104 attack "Coming up next, Mumbai from the west zone." ships person:mumbai (base refuses it); the manifest's "call the base cue first, so they can only narrow" is false for two of the three predicates
evidence: checker u2-4-phase3-resume-c2 cycle 2, lane/ph3 12af112 vs base 536a56a, via extractSpeakers with an injected complete. Layout [spk:1 T, spk:0 "I think so, yes.", spk:1 "ok"], proposal {speakerRef:'spk:0',displayName:N,turnIds:['t1']}: base refuses, lane SHIPS for (N, T) = ("Mumbai", "Coming up next, Mumbai from the west zone.") [recorded ISS-104 attack #18], ("Mumbai", "Welcome to the Mumbai office. Over to you, Mumbai."), ("India", "Over to you, India."). Layout [spk:1 "ok", spk:0 "I think so, yes.", spk:1 T] (thanks route): lane SHIPS for ("Paris", "Thank you, Paris, for hosting us. Our students in Paris were great."), ("Google", "Thank you, Google."), ("Amazon", "Thank you, Amazon."); base refuses. Predicate-level, 30 names x 22 address/handover/thanks templates: 160/660 inputs the lane accepts and the base refuses, including Paris, Mumbai, India, Google, English, Diwali, Delhi, Amazon. End to end over the same grid and four layouts: 432/2640 ship on the lane that the base refused. Mechanism: speaker-relation-rules.ts citesNameAsHandover and citesNameAsThanks call only nameOccurrences/reported/regexes; only citesNameAsSelfIdentification calls hasNamingCueAt (mutation M6, adding hasNamingCueAt to citesNameAsHandover, is killed by speaker-relation-rules.test.ts and speakers-windows.test.ts, so the suite pins the divergence as intended). The manifest's D-015 line "ISS-104 ... 20/20 end to end, no regression" was measured only with the evidence in the SAME turn as the label's speech; the same 20 recorded texts in the preceding-turn layout give 1/20 shipped on the lane (Mumbai) vs 0/20 on the base. Scorer corroboration: ISS255 case 4 fails 12 of 18 evidence pairs on the lane's own replay because those turns do not pass the base cue.
fix_direction: Either make the relation predicates call hasNamingCueAt-equivalent protections that remain valid for a third-party turn (apply readsAsAPlaceOrOrg to the occurrence; keep the closed-class check; add a person-vs-place signal for the handover/thanks occurrence), or hold the handover and thanks routes behind the live gate and ship only self-identification. Add a regression test that replays the recorded ISS-104 texts in the preceding-turn and following-turn layouts and asserts 0/20, and the three place cases above.

title: The ISS-290 corpus lock has no automated test and only notes (does not refuse) positional sessions outside the pin: making verifyCorpus a no-op survives the whole suite
evidence: checker u2-4-phase3-resume-c2 cycle 2: grep finds corpus-lock/verifyCorpus referenced only by 04-regate-eval.mts, 05-score.mjs and corpus-lock.mjs; no *.test.* file. Manual tamper test (temp dir, one appended byte in 2026-08-27-in-focus-4/turns.json) makes both 05-score.mjs and 04-regate-eval.mts throw 'ISS-290: corpus drift -- changed/missing: [2026-08-27-in-focus-4]', but nothing automated would notice a regression of the lock itself. 6 positional sessions are outside the pin (2026-09-02-india-test-series-part2, 2026-09-09-global-test-prep-pathways, 2026-09-16-pathways-in-psychology, 2026-09-21-uniaccess-japan, 2026-09-24-in-focus, 2026-09-24-zoho-next-european-study-destinations) and are printed to stderr only; ISS-290's fix_direction asks to fail loudly and to cover 01-block-stats.mjs, which is untouched.
fix_direction: File-don't-fix per the low-severity rule; a later unit may add a node:test that tampers a temp copy and expects the throw, and decide whether unpinned positional sessions should fail the gate run.

title: The self-identification route ships reported speech, questions and address forms as the speaker's own name ("He said I am Nikhil.", "Do you think I am Nikhil?", "I am, Nikhil, still waiting"), and the lane's block-location citation path makes the model's NEXT-DOOR citation enough to ship them where the base refused
evidence: checker u2-4-phase3-resume-c2 cycle 3, lane/ph3 d5c8912 vs frozen base 536a56a, via extractSpeakers with an injected complete [{speakerRef:L,displayName:'Nikhil',turnIds:[cite]}]. relationGate applies isReportedAt ONLY to the third-party routes (thirdParty ? !isReportedAt : hasNamingCueAt); self-identification gets isQuotedAt (marks only) and the base cue, and hasNamingCue strips commas, so reporting verbs, questions and comma-address pass. Seven recorded reproductions, each also with N in {Rashi,Sumit,Nupur,Priya,Kshitij,Anisha,Jubin,Sonal,Ruby,Makrand Rajadhyaksha,Mumbai Sharma,Doris Day,Prasanti}: (1) "He said I am Nikhil." (2) "She told us, I'm Nikhil." (3) "He said: I am Nikhil, and left." (4) "People go, I am Nikhil, and stall." (5) "I was told my name is Nikhil." (6) "Do you think I am Nikhil?" (7) "I am, Nikhil, still waiting for the slides." Layout A [spk:0 T, spk:0 "I think so, yes.", spk:1 "ok"], proposal spk:0 -> Nikhil citing t2 (the label's own next turn): BASE refuses (t2 does not contain the name), LANE SHIPS spk:0 -> Nikhil for all seven. Layout B [spk:1 T, spk:0 "I think so, yes.", spk:1 "ok"], proposal spk:1 -> Nikhil citing t2: base refuses, lane ships. Cited directly (t1) the base ships all seven too, so the underlying cue defect is inherited; what is new is that the lane turns a refusal into a shipment. Across my extended grid (14 person names + 30 place/org/closed-class names x 56 templates x 7 layouts x 2 labels x every cite, 108,416 cells) the lane ships 8,424 cells the base does not; the non-genuine ones are exactly these seven forms (1,212 cells with person names, plus the same forms with 22 place/org names) and "This is Makrand Rajadhyaksha Sharma's view." for multi-token names; the rest are genuine self-introductions reached through a neighbouring citation. The lane never ships on a label that does not own the text (0 cells; the base ships 7,872 such cells). The committed differential test cannot see this: its TEMPLATES tag only handover/thanks forms as reported (t:'r'), and its allow-list admits any cell where the base accepts the same turn cited directly, which includes the base's own wrong acceptances. Not in any recorded ISS-104/282/PH3-001/002 reproduction: those all measure 0 on the lane.
fix_direction: Apply a reporting/question/address refusal to the self-identification route as well (a reporting verb earlier in the clause or a colon-quote; a clause ending in '?'; a comma between the cue and the name), keeping the ordinary idiom "I would like to introduce myself, I'm Ruby" shipping (the reason the maker exempted it; use a narrower verb list for this route: said|says|told|asked|replied|wrote|mentioned|heard|go|goes|like-as-quotative). Add the seven texts above to the committed grid with t:'r' AND to speaker-relation-ledger.test.ts at layouts own-turn, own-block-other-turn (cite the label's next turn), preceding-turn; and replace the allow-list's 'base accepts same turn directly' premise with 'the occurrence passes an independent oracle of genuine self-identification', so the base's own wrong acceptances cannot license a lane-only shipment.

title: Test and API gaps around relationGate: the differential test alone does not kill 'drop the quoted-speech guard'; the `routes` override argument is public on all three predicates and RELATION_ROUTES is a mutable object, so the OFF state is a default not an invariant
evidence: checker u2-4-phase3-resume-c2 cycle 3. (a) Mutation M4 (gate: `!isQuotedAt(text, at) &&` -> `true &&`) is KILLED by the whole nine-file set (one test in speaker-relation-rules / windows) but SURVIVES speakers-differential.test.ts run alone (fail 0), because the grid's quoted templates are handover/thanks forms and the self-identification quoted forms are absent. (b) relationGate(route, text, name, check, routes = RELATION_ROUTES) and citesNameAsSelfIdentification/Handover/Thanks(text, name, routes?) accept an override; only tests pass it (namingTurns passes none; speakers-llm.ts calls only namingTurns; index.ts exports none of them), so production code cannot reach it today, but nothing stops a later caller. RELATION_ROUTES is typed Readonly but not Object.freeze'd. Mutation 'gate ignores route switch' and 'handover route ON' are both killed.
fix_direction: File-don't-fix per the low rule unless a later unit touches the file: Object.freeze(RELATION_ROUTES); take the override from a test-only seam (or drop it and have tests mutate a copy via a factory); add a quoted self-identification template to the differential grid.
